head: 5b27c69e71e96f29173388f6930c99cba373f11e
verdict: pass (0 blocking, 0 must-fix technical defect found, 10 observations: wording/number consistency in the delivery evidence package, scope/traceability notes, and one wording note on clean-clone portability)

observations.summary: delivery default/features-cuda test baseline is stale: 971/0/364 with 111 binaries vs actual 971/0/369 with 112 binaries
observations.detail: README section 0/2, receipt.three_configs_clean and logs/gates-final.txt say 364 ignored / 111 binaries; the delivery's own .normify/runs/...stage2-r2/unit.json records 971/0/369 and the r2 acceptance baseline is 971/0/369. My clean run: 971/0/369, 112 binaries. Root cause: unit-summary logs have 111 result lines and miss the tests/stage2_equivalence_window.rs binary (0 passed / 0 failed / 5 ignored), added by the same commit.
observations.severity: observation (numbers in narrative wrong; gate record and acceptance correct)
observations.suggested_action: update README section 0/2, receipt and gates-final.txt to 971/0/369 / 112 binaries before the final collection, or mark them as pre-window-test measurements

observations.summary: committed evidence still contains stale 'GPU window 0 / UNC-2 open / equivalence pending' text next to the closed UNC-2 claim
observations.detail: receipt.json (status in_progress, gpu_windows 0, unc2 open, equivalence pending 3b/3c), README header bullet (lines 6-7) and README section 7 last line (line 149) contradict README section 7/7.1 and the window doc. tests/stage2_equivalence_window.rs three_record_summary also hardcodes unc2_closed=false and writes open into three-records.json.
observations.suggested_action: unify receipt/README/header and either update the harness text or add an explicit note that closure is a governance decision recorded in README 7.1

observations.summary: the root cause written for E window exit=101 does not match the raw E log
observations.detail: window doc section 2 attributes the 3 failed CPU record tests to the harness row-order comparison bug. The E log shows the 3 tests failed with 'read dump ... os error 3' because libtest name order ran the dump-producing test last; the row-order bug is the separate ellipsoid run1/run2 raw-array inconsistency. exit=101 itself and 'dumps landed, CPU-only rerun' are truthfully disclosed.
observations.severity: observation (fact of exit 101 disclosed; cause misattributed)
observations.suggested_action: correct the cause sentence and keep both sub-facts (dump ordering; row-order normalization) separate

observations.summary: '9 case dump two runs bit-identical' holds only under the G5 row-order normalization
observations.detail: ellipsoid-box Contact run1/run2 raw arrays differ by row order only (worldid 1,0 vs 0,1, same value multiset); normalized 17/17 dumps are bit-identical (my independent recompute).
observations.severity: observation (window doc section 4 discloses it; the qualifier text does not carry the qualifier)
observations.suggested_action: add the row-order qualifier wherever the two-run equality is cited

observations.summary: record B uses the G5 section 11.2 exclusion asymmetrically for the three primitive-dispatch cases
observations.detail: G5 README section 11.2 names sphere-box-shallow, sphere-box-deep and capsule-box together as primitive_narrowphase dispatch cases excluded from the device ccd comparison. Delivery record B counts sphere-box-shallow as a valid-reference pass (0 failures) and only excludes deep/capsule as reference_not_comparable. My independent recompute reproduces the numbers either way (shallow 15/26 bit, 1 ULP dist, frame 6.985e-8; deep/capsule red).
observations.severity: observation (does not change 'not B full green'; green subset definition is asymmetric)
observations.suggested_action: either classify shallow also as reference_not_comparable, or state that product-device-vs-frozen-probe is a same-recipe comparison acceptable for shallow

observations.summary: delivery sentence 'product binary scan: MJWARP_* zero hits' is factually wrong
observations.detail: default/cuda product exe contains MJWARP_PHYSICS_PTX_DIR and MJWARP_LAUNCHER_BASELINE_DIR (both from unchanged src/runtime/transfer/kernel product code) as well as embedded CUDA source macros MJWARP_G01_EQUIVALENT / MJWARP_FIELD_BATCHES / MJWARP_MOCAP. Seam identifiers are 0 hits and the changed files contain no env reads, so the substantive seam claim holds.
observations.suggested_action: scope the sentence to seam identifiers (and list the pre-existing MJWARP_* env names)

observations.summary: selection layer backend.rs has no product caller
observations.detail: device_permitted/narrowphase_backend_status/device_program are referenced only in src/runtime/backend/tests.rs; the CLI probe path uses runtime::cuda::prepare_device with shared presence probes. This matches the Chief-approved qualifier (default Host, Device explicit) but if the r2 intent sentence about wiring the device entry into the collision narrowphase is read as dispatch wiring, it is not implemented.
observations.severity: observation (scope note; should be registered as migration debt if dispatch wiring is expected in a later slice)
observations.suggested_action: record in the migration-debt list of the delivery README

observations.summary: window/equivalence raw artifacts are not committed
observations.detail: attempt4 logs, 17 product dumps, record-b.json, result.json and three-records.json live only under the gitignored target/stage2-impl/window/; committed evidence has summaries only. On this machine QA could and did recompute them, but a reviewer from the repository alone cannot.
observations.suggested_action: either commit the small record-b.json/result.json summaries or reference the exact machine-local paths in the README (already partly done)

observations.summary: logs/selection-backend-tests-nocuda.log is from an older source layout
observations.detail: it shows unused-import warnings in src/runtime/backend/tests.rs that no longer exist (imports were moved inside the cfg(feature="cuda-probe") module); my no-default clean build has 0 warnings and clippy --no-default-features -D warnings passes (18.5 s, exit 0).
observations.suggested_action: regenerate or drop the stale log

observations.summary: 'clean clone portable' wording is stronger than what a literal Windows git clone can deliver, due to pre-existing EOL-frozen tests
observations.detail: without target/ artifacts: a default-autocrlf clone fails tests/g10_p5_sdf_relmat.rs script-sha (LF-frozen script becomes CRLF), an autocrlf=false clone fails tests/launcher-warp-headers.rs header manifest (frozen from CRLF bytes). Both tests/fixtures already exist at parent commit 54615cd8 and are unrelated to this slice. With a tracked-file copy of the main working tree (exact bytes, no target/, no .git) the default suite is 971/0/369 exit 0, which proves the intended property: no dependency on machine-local target/ frozen artifacts.
observations.severity: observation (pre-existing repo EOL hygiene; scope wording)
observations.suggested_action: say 'no target/ dependency' instead of 'clean clone portable', or register the EOL governance debt
